datasets.title: Climate and Disaster Risk Database at the City-Level for Ethiopia
datasets.description: A comprehensive spatial database containing climate and disaster risk information for Ethiopian secondary cities (above 20,000 inhabitants), combining remote sensing data, earth observation methods, and geodata on climatic and non-climatic hazards to support disaster risk management and urban resilience planning.
datasets.purpose: To identify and map disaster risk at the city level using remote sensing and earth observation methods in combination with the best available geodata for climatic and non-climatic hazards and disaster exposure.

project.name: Ethiopia - Strengthening the Understanding of Urban Disaster Risk in Secondary Cities

datasets.details: This dataset was developed as part of the ACP-EU Disaster Risk Management Program (Component: Improve urban and peri-urban resilience mechanisms) from January 2024 to June 2025. The database includes city-level hazard mapping, urban growth dynamics analysis, and disaster exposure assessments for all Ethiopian urban areas above 20,000 inhabitants. The data supports the establishment of an Urban Observatory and is used by the Ministry of Urban Development and Infrastructure, Ethiopia Space Science and Geospatial Institute, and Ethiopia Disaster Risk Management Commission for evidence-based decision-making on disaster risk reduction and climate adaptation investments.

entity.name: Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery (GFDRR)

sources.name: Fathom 3.0 global flood hazard (RP5, RP20, RP100)
sources.description: Global riverine and pluvial flood hazard model providing flood depth for return periods of 5, 20, and 100 years on ~30 m-90 m grids; for this study, 2030 SSP5-8.5 layers were reclassified into four severity levels (0-3) using flood-depth thresholds.
sources.lineage: Fathom 3.0 flood depth rasters (years 2000-2029, 2030 SSP5-8.5) were clipped to the Ethiopian cities, and depth values for RP5, RP20, and RP100 were recoded into standardized hazard classes: 0 (no flood), 1 (<0.15 m), 2 (0.15-1.0 m), 3 (>1.0 m).

sources.name: Downscaled CMIP6 daily maximum temperature (CCKP)
sources.description: Bias-corrected, downscaled CMIP6 climate projections served through the World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal, providing daily maximum temperature (°C) for multiple scenarios and time slices.
sources.lineage: Daily maximum temperature data for 2000-2029 (SSP5-8.5) from the CCKP were extracted for Ethiopian cities and used to derive annual counts of days above 35°C, 40°C, and 45°C. These indicators were then reclassified into four heat-stress hazard levels (0-3) using percentile-based thresholds tailored to Ethiopian conditions.

sources.name: SPI-3 drought index from ERA5-Land via Global Drought Observatory
sources.description: Global Drought Observatory (GDO) dataset providing Standardized Precipitation Index over 3 months (SPI-3) derived from ERA5-Land reanalysis, used as a proxy for agricultural and meteorological drought.
sources.lineage: Monthly SPI-3 time series (2000-2025) from ERA5-Land, accessed via the Global Drought Observatory, were aggregated for each location. The number of months with SPI-3 below -1, -1.5, and -2 was counted and mapped to a four-class drought hazard scale: 0 (>90% months with SPI-3 > -1), 1 (>=6 months between -1 and -1.5), 2 (>=6 months between -1.5 and -2), 3 (>=6 months < -2).

sources.name: World Bank Global Landslide Hazard Map
sources.description: Global map of rainfall-triggered landslide hazard, providing qualitative classes (negligible to high) based on modeled annual frequency of significant landslides per km².
sources.lineage: The World Bank Global Landslide Hazard Map was clipped to the Ethiopian extent. The original qualitative classes (1-4, negligible to high) were directly recoded into numeric hazard levels: 0 (negligible), 1 (low), 2 (medium), 3 (high) to align with the standardized four-class scheme.

sources.name: Global Seismic Hazard Map (GEM)
sources.description: Global probabilistic seismic hazard map from the Global Earthquake Model (GEM), providing peak ground acceleration (PGA) with 10% probability of exceedance in 50 years on a global grid.
sources.lineage: PGA values with 10% probability of exceedance in 50 years were extracted for the study area and reclassified into four earthquake hazard levels: 0 (PGA < 0.02g), 1 (0.02g-0.1g), 2 (0.1g-0.2g), 3 (>=0.2g), following GEM guidance and regional studies.

sources.name: Global Volcano Hazard Frequency and Distribution
sources.description: Global dataset of volcanic hazard frequency and distribution, summarizing historic explosive activity using the Volcanic Explosivity Index (VEI).
sources.lineage: Historic VEI information from the Global Volcano Hazard Frequency and Distribution dataset was used to assign each volcano and surrounding area to one of four hazard levels: 0 (no historical eruptions), 1 (VEI = 0, effusive), 2 (VEI = 1, severe), 3 (VEI >= 2, explosive and above).

sources.name: GHS-POP-R2023A Global Human Settlement Population
sources.description: Global Human Settlement (GHS-POP-R2023A) gridded population estimates at 100 m resolution for 2000-2020, with projections for 2025 and 2030.
sources.lineage: GHS-POP-R2023A population grids were intersected with city boundaries and hazard layers to estimate the number of people exposed to each hazard class. Population counts were aggregated by city and by standardized hazard severity (0-3).

sources.name: GHS-BUILT-S-R2023A Global Human Settlement Built-up Surface
sources.description: GHS-BUILT-S-R2023A gridded built-up surface dataset at 100 m resolution, describing the fraction of pixel area covered by buildings for 1975-2030.
sources.lineage: Built-up fraction from GHS-BUILT-S-R2023A was overlaid with hazard layers and city boundaries to quantify built-up surface exposed to each hazard class. Indicators derived from this dataset reflect roofed building area rather than total urbanized land, consistent with GHS definitions.

sources.name: Copernicus Digital Elevation Model (DEM)
sources.description: Copernicus DEM providing a global digital elevation model at 30 m resolution (GLO-30) under the Copernicus free and open data policy.
sources.lineage: The Copernicus DEM was used as the reference elevation model for Ethiopia to support derivation and interpretation of flood, landslide, and other natural hazard layers. DEM values were not reclassified into hazard levels but served as an ancillary context layer.

sources.name: CHIRPS daily rainfall
sources.description: Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Station data (CHIRPS), providing quasi-global daily rainfall estimates at ~5 km (0.05°) resolution from 1981 onward.
sources.lineage: CHIRPS daily rainfall was averaged into 5-year periods between 2000 and 2024, plus a long-term mean for 2000-2024, to provide contextual precipitation climatologies supporting the flood and drought analyses.

resources.title: City-Level Hazard Exposure and Urban Growth Indicators for Ethiopia
resources.description: City-level indicators dataset (59 variables) covering built-up surface, population exposure, hazard levels (flood return periods, landslides, heat stress, drought, earthquakes, volcanic hazards), urban growth metrics, and composite exposure indices for Ethiopian cities.
